description: A4f exogenous variable sensitivity — VIX9D/VIX/VIX3M/VVIX + SLOPE + COMBO
motivation: K988/K1056/K1066 all used VIX² as the A4f exogenous regressor. This experiment tests whether VIX9D, VIX3M, VVIX, VIX3M-VIX slope, or a combined specification produces better OOS volatility forecasts on SPY for r²_close and r²_oc targets.
references: K1066: A4f_oc on r²_oc DM t=+7.05

H1_best_exog_vs_VIX.claim: Best A4f-X is Harvey-significantly better than A4f-VIX

H3_best_choice_differs_by_target.claim: Optimal A4f exog is different for r²_close vs r²_oc

H4_theta1_stability.claim: Different VIX variants have different θ₁ CV

paper9_recommendation: KEEP_VIX_BASELINE_ADD_VIX9D_ROBUSTNESS: VIX9D is marginally (Harvey-sig on r²_oc t=3.53, non-sig on r²_close t=2.70) better than VIX, but gain is <0.3% QLIKE and VIX9D has shorter history (2011 vs 1990). Keep VIX as Paper 9 main spec; add VIX9D as robustness appendix showing any VIX-family variable works (content-not-horizon story). SLOPE and COMBO specs offer no additional value.

final_verdict_summary.notes: All four single-VIX variants (VIX, VIX9D, VIX3M, VVIX) Harvey-significantly beat GJR on r²_oc; only VVIX non-sig on r²_close. VIX family works robustly as A4f exog. Specific horizon choice (VIX vs VIX9D) matters only marginally.
